fresh_named_opposition_lp_probes.purpose: Bounded feasibility probes for named constraints that opposed the one-percentage-point lone-parent weight direction.
fresh_named_opposition_lp_probes.constraint_bounds: 0.95 * target <= matrix_row @ weights <= 1.05 * target for every named row.

full_active_uc_evaluation.reason: A zero matrix row cannot reach 95% of its positive target under any permitted weights.

limitations: The first five probes constrain only the ten broad UC counts and the cumulative named non-UC additions; the sixth constrains 108 supported UC/TCL rows plus those same five additions.

The two named positive-target zero-support rows are excluded only from the supported-row LP. They remain in the full 110-row UC evaluation, which is infeasible, and the original canonical terminal-gate refusal is preserved.
The largest subset omits the other 253 active calibration rows. These results do not establish feasibility for all 366 rows or all protected outcomes.
No fixed total household mass or effective sample size constraint is imposed; feasibility does not certify population quality or an acceptable concentration of weights.
Feasibility applies only to the exact named subsets at 5% tolerance and the stated weight bounds; it does not establish exact equality-fit feasibility.
The saved matrix, targets, fresh prior weights and loss coefficients are unchanged. These probes run no new calibration and do not optimize the calibration loss.
LP solution weights are not exported, substituted for calibrated weights or used to create a certified data artifact.
The opposing one-percentage-point direction is direction-specific; the feasible named subsets do not establish that the full calibration objective has no competing priorities.
